primitives.name: Disjoint Union
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2] SETS AND CLASSES 15 A disjoint class is a class E of sets such that every two distinct sets of E are disjoint; in this case we shall refer to the union of the sets of E as a disjoint union.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'class of sets', '∪E': 'disjoint union of sets in E'}
primitives.assumptions: Each pair of sets in E is pairwise disjoint.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sets in E share elements, union is no longer disjoint.

layer2.mapping: Disjoint union corresponds to independent component decomposition in GSI's probabilistic graphical models.
layer2.telemetry: Event independence measure via mutual information between components.

primitives.name: Characteristic Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: If E is any subset of X, the function xE, defined for all x in X by the relations is called the characteristic function of the set E.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\chi_E': 'characteristic function of set E', 'x': 'element of universal set X', 'E': 'subset of X'}
primitives.assumptions: X is a universal set containing all elements under consideration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when x is not in X.

layer2.mapping: Characteristic function enables representation of set membership in GSI's kernel space for similarity computations.
layer2.telemetry: Set inclusion probability derived from kernel evaluation.

primitives.name: Set Operations Distributivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2) Each of the two operations, the formation of unions and the formation of intersections, is distributive with respect to the other, i.e.
primitives.latex: \text{Union distributes over intersection: } A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)
primitives.assumptions: All sets involved belong to the same power set of a universal set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs in non-distributive lattices or improper set definitions.

layer2.mapping: Distributivity mirrors conditional independence in Bayesian networks used by GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Conditional independence test using joint vs product probabilities.

Disjoint unions allow for modular composition of events without overlap, enabling precise modeling of mutually exclusive outcomes. Characteristic functions map set membership into binary-valued functions, facilitating algebraic manipulation and encoding of uncertainty. Set operations like union and intersection exhibit distributive properties which mirror conditional independence in probabilistic reasoning. These primitives collectively support both the symbolic logic required for GSI’s Bayesian inference and the combinatorial state transitions needed for GSE’s dynamic decision-making. The failure mode arises when assumptions about disjointness or closure under operations are violated, leading to inconsistent or undefined behavior in probabilistic models.
